# Analysis plan: effect of BMI on systolic blood pressure

Two-sample Mendelian randomization with summary statistics. Written before any analysis. All data are simulated.

## Question

What is the causal effect of body mass index (BMI) on systolic blood pressure (SBP), in **mmHg per 1 kg/m² higher BMI**?

## Data

`data/main/exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv` (BMI instruments) and `data/main/outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv` (the same variants looked up
in an SBP GWAS). Column definitions, units and coding are in `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

## Steps

1. **Read and clean.** Treat the outcome missing-value code as missing. Drop instruments with no usable outcome data.
2. **Harmonise** every variant so that the exposure and outcome effects refer to the same allele (the exposure effect
   allele). Resolve strand differences by complementing alleles. For palindromic variants (A/T or C/G), infer the strand
   from allele frequency when the minor allele frequency is at most 0.42; otherwise drop the variant. Record the
   harmonisation action for every variant.
3. **Units.** Express exposure effects per kg/m² (1 SD of BMI = 4.8 kg/m²).
4. **Estimate.** Primary: inverse-variance weighted (IVW), multiplicative random effects. Sensitivity: MR-Egger
   (report the intercept) and weighted median. Report Cochran's Q for IVW.
5. **Outputs.**
   - `results/harmonisation_log.csv`: one row per variant, with its harmonisation action and whether it was used
   - `results/estimates.csv`: `method, estimate, se, ci_lower, ci_upper, n_snps`
   - `results/figures/scatter.png`: SNP–outcome against SNP–exposure effects, with the fitted lines
   - `report.md`: at most 200 words for the research group
----
# Data dictionary

> **All data in this folder are SIMULATED** for the IEU AI-for-coding workshop. They describe no real people,
> variants or GWAS. Variant identifiers are synthetic.

## Files

`main/` holds one exposure GWAS file and one outcome GWAS file for the research question.

## `exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv` (exposure: body mass index)

Genetic instruments for BMI from a GWAS of 300,000 people: independent variants (r² < 0.001) associated with BMI at
P < 5×10⁻⁸, pre-selected by the exposure consortium. The exposure consortium does not guarantee which DNA strand
alleles are reported on.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SNP` | Variant identifier |
| `CHR`, `POS` | Chromosome and position (GRCh38) |
| `EFFECT_ALLELE` | Allele whose effect is reported |
| `OTHER_ALLELE` | Other allele |
| `EAF` | Frequency of `EFFECT_ALLELE` |
| `BETA` | Per-copy effect of `EFFECT_ALLELE` on BMI, in **standard-deviation units** (1 SD of BMI = 4.8 kg/m²) |
| `SE` | Standard error of `BETA` (same units) |
| `P` | P-value |
| `N` | Sample size |

## `outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv` (outcome: systolic blood pressure)

Look-up of the BMI instruments in a separate GWAS of SBP (750,000 people, no sample overlap with the exposure GWAS).
Alleles are reported on the forward strand of GRCh38. Some instruments were not available in the outcome GWAS.
**Missing values are coded as `-9`.**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rsid` | Variant identifier |
| `chr`, `pos` | Chromosome and position (GRCh38) |
| `A1` | Reference allele |
| `A2` | Alternative allele. **`beta` and `freq` refer to `A2`** |
| `freq` | Frequency of `A2` |
| `beta` | Per-copy effect of `A2` on SBP, in mmHg |
| `se` | Standard error of `beta` |
| `pval` | P-value |
| `n` | Sample size |
----
     1	# BMI and systolic blood pressure: Mendelian randomization (simulated data)
     2	
     3	**Question.** Causal effect of BMI on SBP, in mmHg per 1 kg/m2 higher BMI.
     4	
     5	**Data.** 100 BMI instruments; 89 used. Dropped: 4 absent from the outcome GWAS, 3 with missing outcome data, 4 ambiguous palindromic variants (MAF > 0.42). Details: `results/harmonisation_log.csv`.
     6	
     7	**Results (mmHg per kg/m2).**
     8	- IVW (random effects): 1.59 (95% CI -0.03 to 3.21)
     9	- Weighted median: 3.29 (95% CI 1.00 to 5.58)
    10	- MR-Egger: 5.42 (95% CI 0.61 to 10.22)
    11	
    12	All estimates are positive, but IVW is imprecise and its interval includes zero. The methods differ considerably, so the size of the effect is uncertain.
    13	
    14	**Heterogeneity and pleiotropy.** Cochran's Q = 135.6 on 88 df (p = 0.00084): clear heterogeneity. MR-Egger intercept = -0.024 mmHg (95% CI -0.052 to 0.004): no clear directional pleiotropy, though the interval is wide.
    15	
    16	**Caveats.** Results rest on MR assumptions these checks cannot prove. Data are simulated; do not interpret as real findings.

# BMI -> systolic blood pressure: two-sample MR (simulated data)

Implements `analysis_plan.md` in base R. Data dictionary: `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

## Rerun
From this folder:

    conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript analysis/mr_analysis.R data/main

(The dataset folder argument is optional; default is `data/main`.) Outputs:
`results/estimates.csv`, `results/harmonisation_log.csv`, `results/figures/scatter.png`.
The script also regenerates a basic `report.md`, overwriting the hand-edited version; the
edited report is the one for the group, so keep a copy before rerunning.

## Headline result
89 of 100 instruments used. IVW estimate: **1.59 mmHg SBP per 1 kg/m2 BMI (95% CI -0.03 to 3.21)**.
Weighted median 3.29 (1.00 to 5.58); MR-Egger 5.42 (0.61 to 10.22), intercept -0.024 (-0.052 to 0.004).
Cochran's Q = 135.6 (df 88, p = 0.00084), so there is notable heterogeneity. The direction is positive in all methods, but
the primary IVW interval includes zero and the methods disagree on magnitude. Data are simulated.
# Notes for AI agents in this project

- All data are simulated. The researcher directs and reviews the work; keep it easy to check.
- Run R as `conda run -n ieu-ai-workshop Rscript <file>`. Base R only: do not install or load add-on packages.
- Analysis code goes in `analysis/`, outputs in `results/`. Use relative paths. Stay inside this folder.
- Quote numbers from the files in `results/`, not from memory.
- Put any scratch or temporary files in `scratch/` inside this folder, not in /tmp.
@AGENTS.md
----
     1	#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
     2	# Two-sample MR: effect of BMI on systolic blood pressure (mmHg per 1 kg/m2).
     3	# Implements analysis_plan.md using base R only.
     4	# Usage (from the project root): Rscript analysis/mr_analysis.R [dataset_folder]
     5	# Default dataset folder: data/main. Outputs go to results/ and report.md in the working directory.
     6	
     7	args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
     8	data_dir <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else "data/main"
     9	
    10	SD_BMI_KGM2  <- 4.8    # 1 SD of BMI in kg/m2 (data dictionary)
    11	MAF_MAX_PAL  <- 0.42   # palindromic variants with MAF above this are dropped
    12	MISSING_CODE <- -9     # outcome missing-value code
    13	set.seed(20240601)     # for the weighted-median bootstrap
    14	
    15	dir.create("results/figures", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    16	
    17	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. Read and clean
    18	exp_file <- file.path(data_dir, "exposure_bmi_gwas.tsv")
    19	out_file <- file.path(data_dir, "outcome_sbp_gwas.tsv")
    20	stopifnot(file.exists(exp_file), file.exists(out_file))
    21	
    22	exposure <- read.delim(exp_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
    23	outcome  <- read.delim(out_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
    24	
    25	# -9 is the outcome's missing code (numeric columns; also guard allele columns)
    26	for (v in c("chr", "pos", "freq", "beta", "se", "pval", "n")) {
    27	  if (v %in% names(outcome)) {
    28	    outcome[[v]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(outcome[[v]]))
    29	    outcome[[v]][!is.na(outcome[[v]]) & outcome[[v]] == MISSING_CODE] <- NA
    30	  }
    31	}
    32	for (v in c("A1", "A2")) outcome[[v]][outcome[[v]] %in% as.character(MISSING_CODE)] <- NA
    33	outcome$A1 <- toupper(outcome$A1); outcome$A2 <- toupper(outcome$A2)
    34	exposure$EFFECT_ALLELE <- toupper(exposure$EFFECT_ALLELE)
    35	exposure$OTHER_ALLELE  <- toupper(exposure$OTHER_ALLELE)
    36	
    37	if (anyDuplicated(exposure$SNP)) stop("Duplicate SNP ids in exposure file")
    38	if (anyDuplicated(outcome$rsid)) stop("Duplicate rsid in outcome file")
    39	
    40	dat <- merge(exposure, outcome, by.x = "SNP", by.y = "rsid", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
    41	dat <- dat[match(exposure$SNP, dat$SNP), ]   # keep exposure order
    42	
    43	in_outcome  <- dat$SNP %in% outcome$rsid
    44	usable_out  <- in_outcome & !is.na(dat$beta) & !is.na(dat$se) & dat$se > 0 &
    45	               !is.na(dat$A1) & !is.na(dat$A2)
    46	
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Harmonise
    48	# Target: outcome effect expressed for the exposure effect allele (EA).
    49	comp <- function(a) c(A = "T", T = "A", C = "G", G = "C")[a]
    50	is_pal <- function(a, b) paste0(sort(c(a, b)), collapse = "") %in% c("AT", "CG")
    51	
    52	dat$action <- NA_character_
    53	dat$flip   <- NA     # TRUE: outcome beta must be negated and freq -> 1 - freq
    54	dat$out_freq_ea <- NA_real_   # outcome frequency of the exposure EA after harmonisation
    55	
    56	for (i in seq_len(nrow(dat))) {
    57	  if (!in_outcome[i]) { dat$action[i] <- "dropped: not in outcome GWAS"; next }
    58	  if (!usable_out[i]) { dat$action[i] <- "dropped: outcome data missing (-9)"; next }
    59	
    60	  ea <- dat$EFFECT_ALLELE[i]; oa <- dat$OTHER_ALLELE[i]
    61	  a1 <- dat$A1[i];            a2 <- dat$A2[i]
    62	  if (!all(c(ea, oa, a1, a2) %in% c("A", "C", "G", "T"))) {
    63	    dat$action[i] <- "dropped: non-ACGT or indel alleles"; next
    64	  }
    65	  # outcome effect is for A2; frequency of EA in outcome if strands agree
    66	  if (is_pal(ea, oa)) {
    67	    if (!(a1 == ea && a2 == oa) && !(a1 == oa && a2 == ea)) {
    68	      dat$action[i] <- "dropped: allele mismatch"; next
    69	    }
    70	    eaf <- dat$EAF[i]
    71	    f_naive <- if (a2 == ea) dat$freq[i] else 1 - dat$freq[i]   # assumes same strand
    72	    if (is.na(eaf) || is.na(f_naive) ||
    73	        min(eaf, 1 - eaf) > MAF_MAX_PAL ||
    74	        min(dat$freq[i], 1 - dat$freq[i]) > MAF_MAX_PAL) {
    75	      dat$action[i] <- "dropped: palindromic, MAF > 0.42 (strand ambiguous)"; next
    76	    }
    77	    same_strand <- (eaf < 0.5) == (f_naive < 0.5)
    78	    if (same_strand) {
    79	      dat$flip[i] <- (a2 != ea)
    80	      dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- f_naive
    81	      dat$action[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), flipped"
    82	                       else "palindromic: same strand (inferred from EAF), no flip"
    83	    } else {
    84	      # opposite strand: outcome A2 is the complement of the allele it appears to be
    85	      dat$flip[i] <- (a2 == ea)
    86	      dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- 1 - f_naive
    87	      dat$action[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), flipped"
    88	                       else "palindromic: strand flipped (inferred from EAF), no flip"
    89	    }
    90	    next
    91	  }
    92	  # non-palindromic
    93	  if (a2 == ea && a1 == oa) {
    94	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "none: alleles aligned"
    95	  } else if (a2 == oa && a1 == ea) {
    96	    dat$flip[i] <- TRUE;  dat$action[i] <- "flipped: allele order swapped"
    97	  } else if (a2 == comp(ea) && a1 == comp(oa)) {
    98	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented, no flip"
    99	  } else if (a2 == comp(oa) && a1 == comp(ea)) {
   100	    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented, no flip"
   101	  } else {
   102	    dat$action[i] <- "dropped: allele mismatch"; next
   103	  }
   104	  dat$out_freq_ea[i] <- if (dat$flip[i]) 1 - dat$freq[i] else dat$freq[i]
   105	}
   106	
   107	dat$used <- !is.na(dat$flip)
   108	dat$beta_out_h <- ifelse(dat$used, ifelse(dat$flip, -dat$beta, dat$beta), NA)
   109	
   110	harm_log <- data.frame(
   111	  SNP = dat$SNP, exposure_EA = dat$EFFECT_ALLELE, exposure_OA = dat$OTHER_ALLELE,
   112	  exposure_EAF = dat$EAF, outcome_A1 = dat$A1, outcome_A2 = dat$A2,
   113	  outcome_freq_A2 = dat$freq, harmonisation_action = dat$action, used = dat$used,
   114	  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   115	write.csv(harm_log, "results/harmonisation_log.csv", row.names = FALSE)
   116	
   117	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Units
   118	# Exposure effects per kg/m2 (data are per SD); outcome already in mmHg.
   119	mr <- dat[dat$used, ]
   120	bx  <- mr$BETA / SD_BMI_KGM2
   121	sex <- mr$SE   / SD_BMI_KGM2
   122	by  <- mr$beta_out_h
   123	sey <- mr$se
   124	n   <- length(bx)
   125	if (n < 4) stop("Too few usable instruments (", n, ") for MR-Egger")
   126	cat(sprintf("%d of %d variants used\n", n, nrow(dat)))
   127	
   128	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. Estimate
   129	z975 <- qnorm(0.975)
   130	
   131	# IVW, multiplicative random effects (residual SE scaled, not allowed below 1)
   132	w <- 1 / sey^2
   133	ivw_fit <- lm(by ~ 0 + bx, weights = w)
   134	ivw_b   <- unname(coef(ivw_fit))
   135	sigma_i <- summary(ivw_fit)$sigma
   136	ivw_se  <- sqrt(1 / sum(w * bx^2)) * max(1, sigma_i)
   137	Q       <- sum(w * (by - ivw_b * bx)^2)
   138	Q_df    <- n - 1
   139	Q_p     <- pchisq(Q, Q_df, lower.tail = FALSE)
   140	I2      <- max(0, (Q - Q_df) / Q)
   141	
   142	# MR-Egger: orient so every SNP-exposure effect is positive
   143	sgn <- sign(bx); sgn[sgn == 0] <- 1
   144	bx_o <- bx * sgn; by_o <- by * sgn
   145	eg_fit  <- lm(by_o ~ bx_o, weights = w)
   146	eg_sum  <- summary(eg_fit)
   147	eg_sig  <- max(1, eg_sum$sigma)
   148	eg_coef <- eg_sum$coefficients
   149	eg_df   <- n - 2
   150	eg_int  <- eg_coef[1, 1]; eg_int_se <- eg_coef[1, 2] / eg_sum$sigma * eg_sig
   151	eg_b    <- eg_coef[2, 1]; eg_b_se   <- eg_coef[2, 2] / eg_sum$sigma * eg_sig
   152	tcrit   <- qt(0.975, eg_df)
   153	
   154	# Weighted median (Bowden 2016), first-order weights, parametric bootstrap SE
   155	wmedian <- function(b, wt) {
   156	  o <- order(b); b <- b[o]; wt <- wt[o] / sum(wt)
   157	  p <- cumsum(wt) - 0.5 * wt
   158	  below <- max(which(p < 0.5))
   159	  b[below] + (b[below + 1] - b[below]) * (0.5 - p[below]) / (p[below + 1] - p[below])
   160	}
   161	ratio    <- by / bx
   162	se_ratio <- sey / abs(bx)
   163	wm_b <- wmedian(ratio, 1 / se_ratio^2)
   164	boot <- replicate(1000, {
   165	  bxs <- rnorm(n, bx, sex); bys <- rnorm(n, by, sey)
   166	  wmedian(bys / bxs, 1 / (sey / abs(bxs))^2)
   167	})
   168	wm_se <- sd(boot)
   169	
   170	estimates <- data.frame(
   171	  method   = c("IVW (multiplicative random effects)", "MR-Egger", "MR-Egger intercept", "Weighted median"),
   172	  estimate = c(ivw_b, eg_b, eg_int, wm_b),
   173	  se       = c(ivw_se, eg_b_se, eg_int_se, wm_se),
   174	  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   175	crit <- c(z975, tcrit, tcrit, z975)
   176	estimates$ci_lower <- estimates$estimate - crit * estimates$se
   177	estimates$ci_upper <- estimates$estimate + crit * estimates$se
   178	estimates$n_snps   <- n
   179	estimates <- estimates[, c("method", "estimate", "se", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "n_snps")]
   180	write.csv(estimates, "results/estimates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
   181	
   182	cat(sprintf("IVW Cochran's Q = %.2f (df %d, p = %.3g), I2 = %.2f\n", Q, Q_df, Q_p, I2))
   183	print(estimates, digits = 4)
   184	
   185	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. Scatter plot
   186	png("results/figures/scatter.png", width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 200)
   187	xlim <- range(c(0, bx_o - z975 * sex, bx_o + z975 * sex))
   188	ylim <- range(c(by_o - z975 * sey, by_o + z975 * sey, 0))
   189	plot(bx_o, by_o, pch = 16, col = "grey30", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim,
   190	     xlab = "SNP effect on BMI (kg/m2 per allele)",

# plus palindromic-rule and word-count checks. Does not use the script's code paths.
d <- read.csv("review/real_harmonisation_independent.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d <- d[d$used, ]
cm <- c(A="T", T="A", C="G", G="C")
# palindromic variants: decide strand by comparing EAF with outcome freq of the labelled A2
pal <- d$pal
f2  <- d$freq                                   # frequency of labelled A2
ea_is_a2 <- d$A2 == d$EFFECT_ALLELE
fEA_same <- ifelse(ea_is_a2, f2, 1 - f2)        # outcome freq of EA if strands agree
same <- (d$EAF < .5) == (fEA_same < .5)
# true allele of A2 in exposure labels: same strand -> A2; opposite -> comp(A2)
true_a2 <- ifelse(same, d$A2, cm[d$A2])
d$my_flip[pal] <- (true_a2 != d$EFFECT_ALLELE)[pal]
d$by <- ifelse(d$my_flip, -d$beta, d$beta)
bx <- d$BETA / 4.8; sx <- d$SE / 4.8; se <- d$se; w <- 1 / se^2
b  <- sum(w * bx * d$by) / sum(w * bx^2)
Q  <- sum(w * (d$by - b * bx)^2); n <- nrow(d)
phi <- max(1, sqrt(Q / (n - 1)))
cat(sprintf("n=%d  IVW=%.3f  se(RE)=%.3f  CI %.2f to %.2f  Q=%.2f (df %d) p=%.3g\n",

            b + 1.96 * phi / sqrt(sum(w * bx^2)), Q, n - 1, pchisq(Q, n - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)))
o <- ifelse(bx < 0, -1, 1); X <- bx * o; Y <- d$by * o
f <- lm(Y ~ X, weights = w); s <- summary(f)
cat(sprintf("Egger slope=%.3f  intercept=%.4f\n", coef(f)[2], coef(f)[1]))

**Do not share this report yet.** One harmonisation bug flips the sign of about a third of the instruments. It changes the headline numbers and reverses the report's conclusions. I did not edit `analysis/`, `results/` or `report.md`; checksums are identical before and after. Everything I made is in `review/`.

## The bug

`analysis/mr_analysis.R:99-100`:
```r
} else if (a2 == comp(oa) && a1 == comp(ea)) {
    dat$flip[i] <- FALSE; dat$action[i] <- "strand: complemented, no flip"   # should be TRUE
```
If the outcome's A2 is the complement of the exposure's **other** allele, the outcome beta is per the other allele and must be negated. Lines 97-98, where A2 is the complement of the effect allele, correctly don't flip. Lines 99-100 copy that branch, and the log lumps both under one label.

It affects 27 of the 85 non-palindromic variants in the real data (`review/check_real.R`).

## 1. Plan against code

| Step | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Read and clean (-9 → missing, drop unusable) | lines 26-32, 43-45, 57-58 | Matches |
| Harmonise (swap, complement, palindromes ≤ 0.42, log every variant) | lines 56-105 | **Mismatch at lines 99-100** |
| Palindromic rule | lines 72-77 | Matches. The code also tests outcome MAF, which is stricter than the plan, but all 4 dropped variants have both MAFs > 0.43 (`independent_mr.R`). |
| Units: per SD → per kg/m² | lines 120-121 (`BETA/4.8`, `SE/4.8`) | Matches the dictionary. The outcome is already in mmHg. |
| IVW with multiplicative random effects, Q | lines 132-139 | Matches |
| MR-Egger with intercept | lines 143-152 | Matches |
| Weighted median | lines 155-168 | Matches |
| Outputs | `estimates.csv`, log, scatter | Present and in the specified format. `report.md` is 160 words, under the 200 limit. |

## 2. Known answer

I simulated 147 instruments with a true effect of 2.0 mmHg per kg/m² and no pleiotropy. The scenarios were:
- aligned, swapped, and both complement cases
- all four palindromic strand/order combinations
- palindromes with MAF above 0.42
- missing `-9` rows
- a `-9` in `freq` only
- instruments absent from the outcome file

I ran the unchanged script from inside `review/` via `review/run_unchanged.R`.

| Run | IVW | Weighted median | Egger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Near noise-free, original script | 1.16 | 2.00 | 1.62 |
| Near noise-free, line 100 patched | 2.000 | 2.000 | 2.000 |
| Realistic noise, original script | 1.39 (0.83 to 1.94) | 1.51 | 2.59 |
| Realistic noise, line 100 patched | 1.79 (1.27 to 2.31) | 1.58 | 0.35 (−1.97 to 2.67) |

- **The original script does not recover the effect.** At realistic noise the true value of 2.0 is outside its IVW interval.
- **Everything else was right** (`review/check_sim.R`): all 20 drops, the `-9` handling, and the palindromic strand inference. The only error is 28 of 127 wrong signs, all in the "complement of the other allele" scenario.
- The patched copy is `review/mr_analysis_fixed.R`, a one-line `diff` from the original.

## 3. Hand check, one real variant per action

| Action | Variant | By hand | Script |
|---|---|---|---|
| not in outcome | rs50795004 | absent from the outcome file | ✓ |
| outcome missing | rs77134306 | beta = −9 | ✓ |
| palindromic, MAF > 0.42 | rs90247876 | EAF 0.52, so MAF 0.48 | ✓ |
| swapped, flipped | rs94071924 | EA=G, A2=A, so beta is per the other allele: negate → −0.0654 | ✓ |
| aligned | rs19369461 | A2=G=EA, no flip → −0.0326 | ✓ |
| palindromic, same strand, no flip | rs49900600 | freq of T 0.103 against EAF 0.117, A2=EA | ✓ |
| palindromic, opposite strand, flipped | rs93437852 | A2 labelled T has freq 0.85 against EAF 0.15, so the true allele is A: negate → −0.0817 | ✓ |
| palindromic, opposite strand, no flip | rs58559743 | labelled G has freq 0.095 against EAF of C 0.107, so the true allele is C: no flip | ✓ |
| **complemented, no flip** | **rs73176882** | EA=C, OA=T, A2=A=comp(T), freq 0.402 ≈ 1−0.594, so beta −0.0573 is per T and the effect per C is **+0.0573** | **✗ script uses −0.0573** |

The log has no "palindromic: same strand, flipped" action, so that one is untested on the real data. The simulation covers it with 0 errors.

An independent frequency check supports this. After my harmonisation the mean gap between EAF and the outcome frequency of the effect allele is 0.009; after the script's it is 0.118.

## 4. Claims in `report.md`

My corrected figures come from the patched copy (`review/real_fixed/`). My from-scratch code reproduces them: IVW 4.773 (3.45 to 6.09), Q 89.94, Egger 7.325.

| Line | Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Question and units | **Release** | |
| 5 | 100 instruments, 89 used, drops 4 / 3 / 4 | **Release** | Log counts match, and all three drop types were hand-checked. |
| 8 | IVW 1.59 (−0.03 to 3.21) | **Revise** | It matches `estimates.csv`, but that file is wrong. Corrected: 4.77 (3.45 to 6.09). |
| 9 | Weighted median 3.29 (1.00 to 5.58) | **Revise** | Corrected: 5.20 (3.15 to 7.26). |
| 10 | MR-Egger 5.42 (0.61 to 10.22) | **Revise** | Corrected: 7.33 (3.39 to 11.26). |
| 12 | "IVW interval includes zero… methods differ considerably" | **Withdraw** | Corrected IVW excludes zero. The three methods are 4.8, 5.2 and 7.3, with overlapping intervals. "All positive" still holds. |
| 14 | Q = 135.6, df 88, p = 0.00084, "clear heterogeneity" | **Withdraw** | The original run gives 135.62, but it is an artefact. Corrected Q = 89.94, p = 0.42, so no evidence of heterogeneity. |
| 14 | Egger intercept −0.024 (−0.052 to 0.004), "no clear directional pleiotropy" | **Revise** | Corrected: −0.016 (−0.039 to 0.007). The conclusion still holds. |
| 16 | Caveats | **Release** | |

The README repeats the same wrong numbers, so it needs the same revision.

## Smaller points (none change the results)
- `results/figures/scatter.png` is drawn from the wrong data and must be regenerated.
- The harmonisation log doesn't record the harmonised beta or sign, which is why this bug was hard to see. Adding that column would make checking easy.
- The script overwrites the hand-edited `report.md` on every run, as the README warns.
- Line 72 would label a palindrome with a missing `freq` as "MAF > 0.42". It doesn't occur in the real data.
- `AGENTS.md` says scratch files go in `scratch/`. I used `review/`, as you asked.

## Needs your decision
Fix line 100 (set `TRUE` and relabel the action), rerun, then rewrite `report.md` and the README from the new `results/` files. I haven't done this because you asked me not to edit those files. The patched copy and the corrected numbers are ready in `review/` if you want to reuse them.
